literal: The prognostication says: "Venus lost its course and went north; this is called 'returning to life.'"
idiomatic: The omen reads: when Venus strays northward, it is termed a reversal of fortune—an ill omen of resurgent violence.

literal: If there is not the destruction of an army, there must be the slaughter of a city.
idiomatic: Either a field army will be shattered or a city will be put to the sword.

literal: " In the fifth month, Ji Sang attacked Ye; Feng Song, the Administrator of Wei Commandery, went out to battle and was greatly defeated; Sang thereupon harmed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan, killed more than ten thousand persons, and burned the palace chambers of the Wei era until all were exhausted.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, Ji Sang struck Ye. Wei’s prefect Feng Song rode out to meet him and was routed. Ji Sang then killed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan, massacred over ten thousand people, and razed the old Wei palaces to ash.

literal: In that year’s ninth month, day dingwei, Mars guarded the Heart [asterism].
idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the ninth month that year, Mars stationed itself in the Heart.

literal: The prognostication says: "The king abhors it."
idiomatic: The omen warns that the sovereign should dread this sign.

literal: " On day jihai, Saturn guarded Fang and the Heart.
idiomatic: On jihai, Saturn stood fixed in Fang and the Heart.

literal: The prognostication says: "When Saturn guards Fang, there is much misfortune and mourning;
idiomatic: The text says Saturn lingering in Fang foretells repeated calamity and bereavement;

literal: when it guards the Heart, there is internal disorder in the state, and the realm is granted amnesty."
idiomatic: when it halts in the Heart, civil strife follows and a general pardon sweeps the empire."

literal: " At this time Sima Yue monopolized power; in the end, because of lack of propriety, he was destroyed and extinguished—this was the correspondence to internal disorder.
idiomatic: Sima Yue had seized the government and, for his arrogance and breach of ritual, was eventually ruined—exactly the domestic turmoil the stars had portended.

literal: In the eleventh month the emperor collapsed; Emperor Huai ascended the throne and greatly pardoned all under Heaven.
idiomatic: The emperor died that November; Huai succeeded and proclaimed a general amnesty.

literal: In the twelfth month, day dinghai, first year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai, stars flowed and shook apart.
idiomatic: On dinghai in the twelfth month of Huai’s Yongjia 1, meteors streaked and burst in showers.

literal: According to Liu Xiang’s explanation, the arrayed lodges of the celestial offices are images of those holding office;
idiomatic: Liu Xiang held that the major constellations mirror men in high position;

literal: those many small stars without names are the category of the common multitude.
idiomatic: the nameless lesser stars stand for the common people.

literal: This is the image that the hundred officials and the common multitude are about to flow and scatter.
idiomatic: Thus the sky foretold the dispersal of officials and populace alike.

literal: After this, all under Heaven was greatly disordered; the hundred officials and the myriad surnames drifted, moved, turned, and died.
idiomatic: Soon the realm descended into chaos; countless officials and families were uprooted and perished on the road.

literal: In the second year, first month, day gengwu, Venus lay hidden and was not seen; in the second month, day gengzi, it first at dawn was seen in the east—this is called ‘ought to be seen yet not seen’; the prognostication is the same as the preceding article.
idiomatic: In year two, Venus vanished on gengwu of the first month and only reappeared at dawn in the east on gengzi of the second—an ‘invisible when expected’ omen matching the earlier rule.

literal: After this, the destruction of armies and the killing of generals were not able to be counted; the emperor collapsed in the barbarian court, and the Central Xia sank and overturned.
idiomatic: There followed uncountable routs and slain commanders; the sovereign died a captive among the nomads, and the heartland fell.

literal: In the third year, first month, day gengzi, Mars encroached upon Purple Subtlety.
idiomatic: On gengzi of the first month of the third year, Mars trespassed into the Purple Palace.

literal: The prognostication says: "There will be a king who dies in the wilds, and moreover there is fire burning the palace."
idiomatic: The omen speaks of a ruler dying away from his capital and of flames consuming the halls.

literal: " At this time the Director of Astronomy Gao Tang Chong submitted a memorial that the imperial carriage ought to remove to another place of fortune; if not, there would certainly be no Luoyang.
idiomatic: Court astronomer Gao Tang Chong urged the throne to flee the capital or lose Luoyang entirely.

literal: In the fifth year, sixth month, Liu Yao and Wang Mi entered the capital city, burned the palace corridors, seized the emperor, and returned him to Pingyang.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year Liu Yao and Wang Mi took the capital, set the palace corridors ablaze, seized the sovereign, and marched him back to Pingyang.

literal: In the third year, Saturn long guarded the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: Through the third year Saturn lingered in the Southern Dipper.

literal: The prognostication says: "Where Saturn dwells long, that state has blessing."
idiomatic: The canon says prolonged Saturn residence brings fortune to the land beneath it.

literal: " At this time the General Who Pacifies the East, the Prince of Langye, first had Yangzhou soil.
idiomatic: Meanwhile the Prince of Langye, General Who Pacifies the East, was first securing his hold on the Yangzhou region.

literal: In that year’s eleventh month, the earth moved; Chen Zhuo took this to be the correspondence of the earth’s moving.
idiomatic: Earth tremors struck that November; Chen Zhuo read them as the terrestrial echo of the omen.

literal: In the fifth year, tenth month, Mars guarded the Heart.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year Mars again stationed itself in the Heart.

literal: In the sixth year, sixth month, day dingmao, Venus encroached upon Supreme Subtlety.
idiomatic: On dingmao of the sixth month of the sixth year Venus crossed into the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

literal: The prognostication says: "Soldiers enter the Son of Heaven’s courtyard; the king abhors it."
idiomatic: The omen warns of troops in the imperial precincts—a thing every ruler fears.

literal: " In the seventh month the emperor collapsed in the bandit court; all under Heaven went in mourning and great lamentation.
idiomatic: The following July the sovereign perished in captivity, and the realm went into deep mourning.

literal: In the first year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan, seventh month, Venus encroached upon the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: In Yuan’s Taixing 1, Venus trespassed the Southern Dipper in the seventh month.

literal: The prognostication says: "In Wu and Yue there will be soldiers; great men will worry."
idiomatic: The text predicts war in the southeast and anxiety among the great.

literal: " In the second year, second month, day jiashen, Mars encroached upon Eastern Well.
idiomatic: On jiashen of the second month of the second year Mars entered the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication says: "Soldiers arise; noble ministers slaughter one another."
idiomatic: The omen foretells mobilization and mutual slaughter among the elite.

literal: " In the eighth month, day jimao, Venus encroached upon the great star of the Coach-and-Courts [of the Purple Palace].
idiomatic: On jimao of the eighth month Venus brushed the great Coach-and-Courts star.

literal: The prognostication says: "The rear palace worries."
idiomatic: The wives’ quarters were warned of trouble ahead.

literal: " In the third year, fifth month, day 己戊子 (scribal corruption), Venus entered Supreme Subtlety and moreover encroached upon the star of the upper general.
idiomatic: In the third year's fifth month, on the wuzi day, Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and struck the senior general's star (戊子; the received text 己戊子 is corrupt).

literal: The prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven himself will lead troops; the upper general is executed."
idiomatic: The omen speaks of the emperor taking the field and a top commander paying with his life.

literal: " In the ninth month, Venus encroached upon the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: That September Venus again crossed the Southern Dipper.

literal: In the tenth month, day jihai, Mars was in Eastern Well, dwelling south of the Five Feudal Lords, hesitating and lingering, staying and accumulating thirty days.
idiomatic: From jihai in the tenth month Mars lingered in the Well south of the Five Feudal Lords, dawdling there a full month.

literal: The prognostication says: "When Mars guards the Well twenty days or more, great men worry."
idiomatic: The canon says Mars tarrying in the Well beyond twenty days alarms the mighty.

literal: When it guards the Five Feudal Lords, among the feudal lords there is one who is executed.
idiomatic: If it halts on the Five Feudal Lords, one regional lord will be put to death.

literal: " In the third month of first year of Yongchang, Wang Dun led the hosts of Jiang and Jing to come attack the capital city; the Six Armies resisted in battle, were defeated and routed; the human ruler apologized for fault only.
idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 Wang Dun marched the Jing–Jiang armies on the capital; the imperial host was beaten, and the emperor could only offer a humiliating apology.

literal: Thereupon they killed General Who Guards the Army Zhou Yi, Director of the Secretariat Diao Xie, and General Who Gallops as Swiftly as the [Biao] Cavalry Dai Ruosi.
idiomatic: Zhou Yi, Diao Xie, and Dai Ruosi—champion general, chief minister, and swift cavalry commander—were then executed.

literal: Moreover, General Who Garrisons the North Liu Wei went out and fled.
idiomatic: Liu Wei, General Who Garrisons the North, also fled the court.

literal: In the fourth month, moreover they killed the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince of Qiao, Sima Cheng, and General Who Garrisons the South Gan Zhuo.
idiomatic: The next month Prince Cheng of Qiao, Xiang’s governor, and southern garrison commander Gan Zhuo were slain as well.

literal: In the intercalary twelfth month the emperor collapsed.
idiomatic: The emperor died in the leap twelfth month.

literal: In the third year of Emperor Ming’s Taining, first month, Mars went retrograde and entered Supreme Subtlety.
idiomatic: Early in Ming’s Taining 3 Mars backed into the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

literal: The prognostication says: "There are soldiers and mourning; the king abhors it."
idiomatic: The omen promises war, bereavement, and royal dread.

literal: " In the intercalary eighth month the emperor collapsed.
idiomatic: He died in the leap eighth month.

literal: After two years, Su Jun rebelled, attacked and burned the palace chambers; the Empress Dowager, because of worry and pressure, collapsed; the Son of Heaven was secluded and seized at Stone Fortress City; near and far soldiers were disordered; only in the fourth year did it cease.
idiomatic: Two years later Su Jun rose, torched the palaces, and drove the empress dowager to her death; the young sovereign was held hostage at Stone City while fighting raged until it finally subsided in the fourth year.
